team-wiki-home.title: Team wiki home
team-wiki-home.body:
Northstar engineering wiki

Start here. Everything the team needs on the first day and most of what it needs after.

How we work
- Meeting notes live under Meeting notes, one page per meeting, newest first.
- The roadmap is one page per quarter. Q4 2026 is the current one.
- Every incident gets a retro page within three working days.
- Decisions are written down where they were made, then linked from here.

Pages in this workspace
- Onboarding checklist (start here if you are new)
- Q4 2026 roadmap
- OKRs 2026 H2
- Meeting notes 2026-09-14
- Weekly retro 2026-09-11
- Interview loop
- Reading list
- Recipe collection (not work, still popular)
- Travel plan: Lisbon offsite

Code lives at http://github.com/northstar/atlas and the public site is http://northstar.example/

q4-2026-roadmap.title: Q4 2026 roadmap
q4-2026-roadmap.body:
Q4 2026 roadmap
Owner: Carol. Last reviewed 2026-09-12.

Theme: replay everywhere.

Committed
1. Renderer text layout v2 (Alice) - kerning, hyphenation, vertical rhythm. Ships in 0.5.0.
2. Browser session replay from snapshot (Alice, Bob) - page state, history and forms survive a round trip.
3. Windows on the default CI matrix (Bob) - every test, every platform, no exceptions list.
4. Onboarding in one day (Carol) - a new engineer runs the world and ships a change by end of day one.

Stretch
5. Map service with deterministic routing.
6. Public docs site refresh.

Not doing this quarter
- Multi-machine snapshots. Design first, build in Q1.
- A GUI for the debugger. The CLI is fine and the people who want a GUI want it for demos.

Risks
- Text layout v2 touches every golden image. Regeneration is a day of CI.
- Hiring pace: two open roles; if neither closes by November, item 4 slips.

onboarding-checklist.title: Onboarding checklist
onboarding-checklist.body:
Onboarding checklist
For your first week. Tick things off on your own copy; ask in the team channel if anything is stale.

Day 1
- [ ] Laptop, accounts, keys. IT ticket is filed by your manager before you start.
- [ ] Clone http://github.com/northstar/atlas and run the world: cargo run -p computerworld --example company
- [ ] Read the wiki home and this page. Skim the Q4 roadmap.
- [ ] Ship something: fix a typo in the docs and open a pull request.

Day 2-3
- [ ] Pair with Alice on the renderer for an hour; pair with Bob on CI for an hour.
- [ ] Run the behaviour suite and read one failing-test postmortem end to end.
- [ ] Set up your dotfiles; several people keep theirs in public repositories.

Day 4-5
- [ ] Pick a starter issue from the Onboarding project in Linear.
- [ ] Add yourself to the interview loop as a shadow.
- [ ] Write down what confused you this week. That list becomes an edit to this page.

Rules that will save you time
- No wall clock, no ambient randomness. Time is the tick you were handed.
- Anything unordered is a bug waiting for the Windows runner.

reading-list.title: Reading list
reading-list.body:
Reading list
Add a line, initial it. Rough order of usefulness for our work.

Deterministic systems
- "Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System" - the paper under everything we do. (AC)
- FoundationDB's simulation testing talk - the model for our harness. (AC)
- The Antithesis blog on deterministic hypervisors. (BM)

Rendering and text
- "Digital Typography" chapters on line breaking. Our v2 layout follows the dynamic-programming approach. (AC)
- The Unicode line breaking annex, UAX #14, read once and then keep open. (AC)

Testing
- "Lessons from Building Static Analysis Tools at Google" - on the cost of a false positive. (BM)
- Hypothesis documentation, especially the section on shrinking. (BM)

Management and process
- "An Elegant Puzzle" - the chapter on team sizes. (CN)
- "Debugging Teams" - short, mostly right. (CN)

Wikipedia rabbit holes that turned out to matter
- http://en.wikipedia.org/ - Rayleigh scattering (why the render tests use a blue sky), Knocker-upper (unrelated, delightful).

recipe-collection.title: Recipe collection
recipe-collection.body:
Recipe collection
Things people have brought to the office and been asked for the recipe. Add yours.

Alice's weeknight dal
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed. 3 cups water. Simmer 15 minutes with turmeric and salt.
- Separately fry cumin seeds, a sliced onion, garlic and ginger in ghee until golden. Add a chopped tomato.
- Pour the fry into the lentils, simmer 5 more minutes, finish with lemon and coriander.
- Serves 3, or 1 engineer for two days.

Bob's overnight oats
- Equal parts rolled oats and milk (any), a spoon of yogurt, a pinch of salt.
- Stir, refrigerate overnight. Top with whatever fruit is going soft.
- The pinch of salt is not optional.

Carol's cardamom knots (from the bakery on Hawthorne, reverse engineered)
- Enriched dough: 500 g flour, 250 ml warm milk, 75 g butter, 60 g sugar, 7 g yeast, 1 egg, salt.
- Knead 10 minutes, rise 1 hour. Roll into a rectangle, spread with butter, sugar and ground cardamom, fold, cut into strips, twist into knots.
- Second rise 45 minutes. Bake at 200 C for 12 minutes. Brush with syrup while hot.
- Why bread rises, for the curious: yeast makes the gas, gluten makes the balloon.

Office rules
- Label it. Date it. If it is not yours, ask.

okrs-2026-h2.title: OKRs 2026 H2
okrs-2026-h2.body:
OKRs, second half of 2026
Reviewed monthly. Scores are 0.0 to 1.0; 0.7 is a good result.

Objective 1: A run replays anywhere.
- KR1: Every behaviour test passes on Linux, macOS and Windows with no platform exceptions. (current 0.9)
- KR2: A failure from CI replays locally from its seed in under a minute, ten out of ten tries. (current 0.6)
- KR3: Zero flaky tests in the suite for thirty consecutive days. (current 0.3, streak at 11 days)

Objective 2: The renderer is something we would show a designer.
- KR1: Text layout v2 shipped behind a flag by 1 November. (current 0.5)
- KR2: Golden images regenerated on every platform with a diff of zero. (current 0.4)

Objective 3: New engineers are productive in a day.
- KR1: Onboarding checklist completed by the two September hires in one day each. (current 0.5, one hire, one day)
- KR2: Interview loop rewritten around a debugging exercise; all interviewers trained. (current 0.7)

Notes
- KR 1.3 reset twice in August. Both times it was a test that read the clock.

interview-loop.title: Interview loop
interview-loop.body:
Interview loop - engineering
Updated 2026-09-14. Owner: Carol. Every interviewer reads this before every loop.

Stages
1. Recruiter screen (30 min). Motivation, logistics, compensation range.
2. Technical screen (45 min, remote). One interviewer. The candidate debugs a small failing test in a repository we send an hour ahead. We are watching how they narrow it down, not whether they finish.
3. Take-home (optional, 3 hours cap). Extend a tiny simulator with one feature. Rubric page in progress.
4. Onsite loop (half day):
   - Debugging session (90 min, two interviewers). A recorded failure, a repository, a seed. Same format as the screen, larger problem.
   - Design conversation (60 min). Something we actually built; the candidate is asked what they would do differently.
   - Team conversation (45 min). No puzzles. How they work, how they disagree.
   - Manager conversation (30 min).

Rules
- No whiteboard algorithms. We stopped in 2025 and hiring got better.
- Write feedback before reading anyone else's. Submit within four hours.
- Every candidate gets a decision within three working days of the onsite.

What we are looking for
- Narrows a problem before touching it.
- Says "I do not know" and then finds out.
- Can explain a thing they built to someone who did not build it.

comments.author: bob
comments.text: The debugging screen finds more signal in 45 minutes than the old algorithms round did in two hours.

weekly-retro-2026-09-11.title: Weekly retro 2026-09-11
weekly-retro-2026-09-11.body:
Weekly retro - Friday 11 September 2026
Facilitator: Bob. Fifteen minutes, three columns.

Went well
- 0.4.2 shipped on the day we said. Release notes went out with it.
- The Windows runner is green and has been for eleven days. Nobody had to think about it.
- The new onboarding page got a new engineer to a merged pull request before lunch.

Did not go well
- Text layout golden images regenerated three times because of a font cache on one CI runner.
- A meeting about the roadmap ran forty minutes over. The agenda had six items; two would have done.
- We found out about a customer's replay issue from a forum post rather than from them.

Try next week
- Pin the font cache in the CI image (Bob).
- Two-item agendas for anything under an hour (Carol).
- A support address on the status page that actually reaches an engineer (Alice).

Shout-outs
- Alice, for the layout rewrite reaching the whole handbook.
- Whoever labelled the office fridge. It worked.
